triples.quote: But he had at home an old silver watch which had long ceased to go.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: When Mitya began to speak of his quarrel with his father over his inheritance, the priest was positively alarmed, as he was in some way dependent on Fyodor Pavlovitch.

triples.subject: Gorstkin
triples.quote: he was now at Suhoy Possyolok, that he was staying the night in the forester’s cottage, as he was buying timber there too.

triples.subject: Dmitri Karamazov
triples.quote: He roused him with a sort of ferocity, pulled at him, pushed him, even beat him; but after five minutes of vain exertions, he returned to his bench in helpless despair, and sat down.

triples.subject: Dmitri Karamazov
triples.quote: I’ll pay you for the light,” he said to the forester, “for the night’s lodging, too; you’ll remember Dmitri Karamazov.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: I’m Lieutenant Dmitri Karamazov, the son of the old Karamazov whose copse you are buying.

triples.subject: Lyagavy
triples.quote: “No, you show me this: you tell me the law that allows roguery. D’you hear? You’re a scoundrel! Do you understand that?”

triples.subject: Lieutenant Dmitri Karamazov
triples.quote: And if it had not been for the thought of Grushenka and of what might have happened to her, which never left him, he would perhaps have become quite cheerful again....
